newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross cautiously optimistic in Peru crisis.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross cautiously optimistic in Peru crisis.

text.p: International Red Cross officials on Sunday welcomed the first face-to-face talks between Peru's government and Marxist rebels over the hostage crisis but warned an early solution was not guaranteed.

"The fact that members of the guerrillas and representatives of the government met does not mean the problem is simple. It doesn't mean that at all," Michel Minnig, chief representative of the Red Cross in Lima, said in a television interview. "It means that discussions are starting and disagreement is still there."

In the first direct negotiation between the Peruvian government and guerrillas, Education Minister Domingo Palermo spent more than three hours inside the Japanese ambassador's home on Saturday where about 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels were holding 103 VIP hostages.
Shortly after he left, the rebels freed 20 of their captives leaving 83 inside.

"A government representative has entered the residence, he has talked to the rebels and then hostages have been freed. These are all positive signs and we think that if this momentum can be maintained it could eventually lead to a solution," Red Cross spokesman Ronald Bigler said.

Until Saturday's meeting, Minnig and his team had been the main channel of contact between the MRTA and the government. Palermo was named as the government's chief negotiator early in the crisis but had not previously entered the residence.
"It's an important step ... but there is still a long way to go," said Bigler.
Red Cross officials stressed that the atmosphere inside the residence was calm and that there were no serious health problems among the remaining hostages.
